description: Fictional English community workshop review with corrected counts and costs, accessibility measurements, a late participant and unapproved items.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's check the workshop arrangements. We expect forty eight visitors, and the session runs from ten in the morning until one.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Two visitors cancelled, leaving forty six. Add four volunteers.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks. That makes fifty people, including all four volunteers. Use fifty on the room plan and remove the earlier estimate from every copy.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: The supplier quoted for sixty chairs. I can reduce the order to fifty, but they need the final count before four this afternoon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Can we keep two spare chairs near the entrance? Moving a whole row during the session would be awkward.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, order fifty two chairs. Fifty are allocated places, and two are spares. The expected number of people stays fifty.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Can I pause there? The delivery form says the side entrance, but that door has a step. We should route the trolley through the main entrance.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll mark the ramp route through the main entrance and keep the space beside the door clear.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Measure the passage by the coat rack. We need at least thirty six inches of clear space after setup.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: I measured thirty four inches yesterday. Moving the coat rack against the far wall gives us thirty eight, so I'll change that part of the layout.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll check after setup. Chairs can drift into the passage, so the drawing isn't enough.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For drinks, provide water and tea. We don't have lunch approval, so nobody should order food on the assumption it's included.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Understood. I'll confirm the chairs today and check the passage on Friday afternoon. The supplier can deliver Friday at two rather than Saturday morning.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Friday at two works. I'll arrange for a volunteer to receive the delivery and check the ramp before unloading.

turns.speaker: D
turns.text: I've just joined. I can confirm the hearing support equipment is available, but I need the room layout before I can decide where to place it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We'll send today's revised layout. The entrance route and chair count have changed, so please replace the earlier attachment.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Does the equipment need a power socket, or can it run for the full session without being plugged in?

turns.speaker: D
turns.text: It should run on batteries, but please reserve a nearby socket as backup. I'll test the actual unit on Friday and report any problem before five.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thank you. We'll leave that item open until the test result arrives. We can't assume the equipment will work.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: One last point: the delivery charge is ninety dollars, not nineteen. I misread the quote, and I'll correct that number before requesting approval.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Correct the quote first. The chair order can proceed, but the delivery charge needs approval. Keep those decisions separate.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll update the signs and verify passage width. That's fifty allocated seats, two spare chairs, and no lunch.

turns.speaker: D
turns.text: I'll send the equipment test result on Friday before five. If it fails, I'll include an alternative, but we haven't selected that alternative yet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's the plan. Delivery approval and the equipment test remain open. Everything else has an owner and a clear next step.
